statement_en: Let $g_d(n)$ be minimal such that every collection of $g_d(n)$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ determines at least $n$ many distinct distances. Estimate $g_d(n)$. In particular, does\[\lim_{d\to \infty}\frac{g_d(n)}{d^{n-1}}\]exist?
statement_lean:
open scoped Finset
variable {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X]
noncomputable def distanceSet (points : Finset X) : Finset ℝ :=
  points.offDiag.image fun (pair : X × X) => dist pair.1 pair.2

open scoped Finset
variable {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X]
noncomputable def distinctDistances (points : Finset X) : ℕ :=
  #(distanceSet points)

open scoped Finset
variable {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X]
variable (X) in
noncomputable def minimalDistinctDistances (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {m : ℕ | ∃ points : Finset X, #points = n ∧ distinctDistances points = m}

open Filter
open scoped Topology

noncomputable def g (d n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {m : ℕ | n ≤ minimalDistinctDistances (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) m}

theorem erdos_21665 :
    ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → ∃ L : ℝ,
      Tendsto (fun d : ℕ => (g d n : ℝ) / (d : ℝ) ^ (n - 1)) atTop (𝓝 L) := by
  sorry
